thread.title: Buy Netflix on Recent Sell-Off: Oppenheimer | Investopedia

author: investopedia.com
title: Buy Netflix on Recent Sell-Off: Oppenheimer | Investopedia
text:
Take the opportunity to grab shares of Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) while they're still cheap, recommends one market watcher who expects the on-demand streaming giant to make a comeback after falling into a correction this month.
(For more, see also: Goldman: Wall Street is Underestimating Netflix. )
Investors 'Rotate Out of High Flyers', At Least in the Near-Term While the Los Gatos, Calif.-based FAANG company saw its stock close up nearly 2% on Monday at $355.71, the stock is still down approximately 16% from its June high.
Ari Wald, head of technical analysis at Oppenheimer, spoke on CNBC's "Trading Nation" on Monday, suggesting that Netflix's recent weakness should not concern investors too much. Netflix shareholders have become accustomed to meteoric returns, with the stock jumping 100% higher in the first six months of 2018, and Wald noted that the streaming service is still one of the best performers year-to-date (YTD) . Monday's close reflects a whopping 85.3% return YTD, compared to the S&P 500's 7.7% increase over the same time.
"Whats going on here is there's some rotation out of the high flyers, at least from a year-to-date basis. The stock is one of the worst performers month-to-date," said Wald, who then consulted a technical chart tracking Netflix's growth over time.
"Looking at a chart of Netflix, here's a stock still making higher lows and higher highs, still above a rising 200-day moving average as well. We can make the case that this weakness is still within the uptrend," said the Oppenheimer analyst.
Wald indicated that he is watching two key levels for Netflix's moving average, around $323 per share and $311.
But not every analyst is as upbeat. Gina Sanchez, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Chantico Global, chimed in on the CNBC segment, warning that Netflix's weakness could reflect heightened competition in the streaming sector from players like Walt Disney Co. ( DIS ) and Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), as well as rising pressure on high-multiple tech stocks like Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) and Facebook Inc. ( FB ). She expects the increasingly negative sentiment on the Street to disproportionately weigh on the FAANGs, as Netflix battles with decelerating growth in the U.S. among other issues.
(See also: Why Credit Suisse Sees NFLX Climbing to $470. )
